- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0.05) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 10-day moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 3-day negative sentiment window.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day after day 7.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.17, -0.28, +0.11), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend magnitude (e.g., if sentiment avg = +0.15, forecast should slope up 0.1–0.2% per day).
